The mutation journal records the edit with actor, scope, command, and checkpoint lineage.
The reactive graph republishes the edited buffers and tree as current truth.
Diagnostics correlate the published edit with its command and journal lineage.

drills.title: Support repair reports recovery only after the journal commits

flows.notes: AI apply publishes through the command and journal path; the preview cannot outvote the canonical edit.
flows.parity_rationale: The inline preview is gated and never becomes user-visible truth on its own; if the apply command or journal disagree it reverts to the canonically published edit, so the surface cannot win with a private optimistic cache.
flows.publication_summary: An AI scoped apply shows its edit set as a quarantined pending preview and marks the change current only after the apply command and the mutation journal commit and the reactive graph republishes the edited buffers and tree.

flows.notes: Review actions wait for canonical publish; a moved base or denied approval holds rather than faking approval.
flows.parity_rationale: Approve and merge depend on exact current state; holding in an explicit waiting state until the canonical path publishes prevents a stale base or denied approval from being shown as an approved cache win.
flows.publication_summary: A review approve or merge never optimistically flips the workspace; it waits while the action command and the mutation journal commit, then shows the merge-queue state the reactive graph republishes.

flows.notes: Scaffold/update reflects the canonically published tree only; the old optimistic write was removed.
flows.parity_rationale: The removed optimistic write can no longer diverge from disk; a divergent canonical outcome reverts to the published tree so the file explorer never shows files the journal did not record.
flows.publication_summary: A scaffold or template update shows a pending in-flight cue after its former optimistic tree write was removed, and reflects the new files only once the scaffold command and the mutation journal commit and the reactive tree republishes.

flows.notes: Provider mutation publishes the accepted config; a rejection degrades rather than holding a stale optimistic value.
flows.parity_rationale: A provider can reject a change; degrading to an explicit failed-change state instead of keeping a removed optimistic config prevents the surface from claiming a configuration the provider never accepted.
flows.publication_summary: A connected-provider configuration change shows a pending cue and publishes the new provider state only after the mutation command and the mutation journal commit and the reactive provider surface republishes.

flows.notes: Notebook results publish through the command and journal path; a running cue never stands in for the result.
flows.parity_rationale: A running cue is not a result; holding until the canonical result publishes keeps a cancelled or superseded run from leaving a stale optimistic output behind.
flows.publication_summary: A notebook cell run shows a quarantined running cue and presents the result as current only after the execution command and the mutation journal commit and the reactive graph republishes the cell output.

flows.notes: Support repair waits for canonical publish; a failed repair degrades rather than reporting a cache win.
flows.parity_rationale: A repair can fail partway; degrading to an explicit failed-repair state rather than reporting success keeps the support surface from claiming a recovery the journal never recorded.
flows.publication_summary: A support-center repair never optimistically reports recovered state; it waits while the repair command and the mutation journal commit, then shows the repaired state the reactive graph republishes.

invariants: User-visible state on a mutating surface is published only after the command and the mutation journal commit and the reactive graph republishes; no surface claims success before publication.

No mutating surface keeps a private optimistic cache that can outvote the canonical command, approval, or journal outcome; optimistic paths are never offered as truth, removed, or quarantined behind the publication gate.
Every published state preserves actor, scope, command, and checkpoint lineage so diagnostics and support packets can reconstruct what the user saw and when.
Known divergence cases convert to an explicit degraded or waiting state instead of a hidden cache win.
Each mutating surface publishes through the one canonical reactive path instead of inventing a private epoch or stale-state language.
title: Command-graph and mutation-journal publication parity for mutating surfaces
